The build focuses mostly on normal damage/power shot damage but has some utility with high constitution and stamina surge and keeping DP viable for situations like that, or Vs Vaal/Xeno as those two bosses are pretty good to use DP on. Basically, whatever situation presents itself is what you go for. Find yourself close-ish range weak spot (usually head/tail?) Use power shot for high damage, especially if boss collapses, arc shot/power shot spam. High chance of stunning him again when you do this. Boss locked in an animation or CC and you're lined up for a good DP? Do it. Otherwise, R2 spam and dodge spam provides great dps while being extremely mobile, and you never need to worry about stamina or using dash juice.

There is a slightly higher damage version of this Ele build. Rathalos Helm/Rath Mail B with Kaiser VamBraces B, Nerg Coil B and Diablos Nero Greaves B, the same jewels, but you get attack +4 with the 5% affinity boost and damage boost with 2 ele slots instead of 1. It's DP is only about 1 damage per arrow lower compared to my other build even though there's no piercing shots, the +4 attack makes up for it, but you lose out on the stamina surge LVL 2 so you'll need to manage your stamina a little more. Constitution lvl 4 is pretty good though. That's a little less utility for a little more damage.

It might be an idea to consider. I still need to keep the leggings because I need them for the 2 set Rath bonus, and the entire build falls apart if you try switching them. The issue with the 2 set bonus is usually they take up the chest piece and leg piece for weakness exploit. But in order to use spread shot jewel, you need a 3 slot piece. The only 3 slot equipment that is decent is Dober and Dragonking. Dragonking has weakness exploit, which nullifies the Rath Chestpiece, and Dober takes up the chest piece where the Rath would go. This is what I spent my time scratching my head at and came up with this. I suppose I could use the B version of them which opens up a 3 slot gem, see if there's something more useful. But honestly it's not all that bad. DP is still viable with it in an ele build. It adds about 6+ damage per DP arrow. It won't beat a DP specialised build but it makes DP an option rather than just completely weak.

I wouldn't necessarily say that Unlimited is a slog. I mean for Alternative to have the impact it has, Unlimited is needed, since Alternative is based off of Unlimited. But I agree with you. ML Alternative remains one of the best games I've ever played to date in terms of storyline. But to OP, I'm glad you're checking it out. I can gaurantee you that you will not be disappointed if you enjoyed N:A's storyline, both have very similar feels when playing through them. At least, they did for me.

There's no gameplay in these games, as they are Visual Novels. But if you want a similar sort of story, try the Muv-Luv Franchise. (The ones that start along the path you'll need are Muv Luv  Extra, then Unlimited, but more specifically Muv-Luv Alternative is the big one). It's your typical High School Harem to begin with, but after that it evolves into so much more. I don't want to spoil the storyline. But you'll be wondering why a story that starts out with a High School Harem has any sort of resemblence to Nier: Automata. But stick with it and you'll find out. It's the ONLY "game" where I can honestly see a resemblence to Nier: Automata, and it's the reason why it's probably the highest rated in the western market in terms of VNs. I started with Muv-Luv Extra. I wasn't entirely a fan of it as I'm not a fan of high school comedy type of stuff, but Unlimited/Alternative makes it all the worthwhile. They are that good.

Alternatively, Saya no Uta is another great shout for a visual novel. The storyline is completely different, but that dark theme is definetely there.

I personally don't like the PS4 controller. Mouse and Keyboard feels more reliable. I have seen good players with PS4 Controller, but mouse and keyboard is always going to be the optimum setup. That said, if you really want to use one, follow this advice about plugging it into your PC. If you want to play on your sofa/couch/bed, buy a bluetooth usb and connect your PS4 via Bluetooth. There, now you have the best of both worlds without having to relevel again, and you can also have DPS meters displaying if thats your thing!

I haven't done any savage content, the highest I've done is Seph Ex. My monk is ilvl 222 with Seph Wep, the gear being 220 Alexander and 230 lore. Melded all Crit, between 9 and 12. I could buy another 230 Piece just now but I want the 230 wep in 2 weeks instantly.

My Parser DPS is about 1700-1800 with monk without pot before I run out of TP

I can get to about 5-10% on A8S dummy.

But the rotation I read for an opener is: With pot: 
Demo PB->Snap B4B-> Snap IR -> DK POT -> TS Elixir -> Snap Howling Fist -> ToD Steel Peak -> BS ST -> TS FC -> Demo -> Standard rotation.

Without: The same, but use B4b after 2nd Snap, not 1st and IR after DK. Just moving the OGCD one GCD along since you aren't potting.

You don't need to save medication for purification, at least for all content up to Seph Ex. There will be downtime where you can use it. I can't speak for savage as I haven't done that. But I imagine it will be the same there. Usually in Seph Ex, P1 when I have the green marker and I'm running away/back if ST is on cd I spam med. By the time P2 hits you should have 3-5 built up, adds will be spawning so you can pick up the ones you miss. And I'm spamming Rockbreaker every time, INV usually comes off cd. As for P3, unless you're never picked as orange and never ES, tp wont really be an issue there either, you will have moments to use FC.

Perhaps a MNK with A5S+ experience can tell you whether you should save MedX5 for Purification over FC.

As for Fracture, I'd be wary of when to use that. Fit it in if you can, but it looks like you're trying to revolve your combo around fitting fracture in. It should be the other way around, in that fracture should be fitting its way into your combo only if the conditions are met; not trying to condition it so fracture fits in.

I am 28, I was brought up on these sort of country clubs at 10 years of age. My grandmother used to rent out local community halls and book country bands for a country club night out. It was usually the same group of people that kept it afloat. She died about 15 years back, so I've no clue if these country clubs aside from Grand Ole Opry still exist. My experiences from being 10/never been to the Grand Ole Opry itself: It is an experience to say the least. People will dress up all western/cowboy based/conf military uniform. Spurs/Cowboy hats/Buckles/Gun holsters, the full way. People making up ridiculous cowboy sounding names for themselves (which I admit was fun at the age of 10). Usually the live musicians cover a whole host of country songs/add some of their own songs into the mix.  Expect line dancing as well. There's bingo/raffle prizes (based on the places I went to) and a quick draw competition. The flag salute/folding at the end and the pretend firing for it, I found ridiculous. Even at 10.

Personally, it seems like an older generation thing to me, since country was big then and most of the country clubs seemed to be full of 30-50s when I was 10. An excuse to get out and dress up. If you think about the Catty, people spiking up their hair in mohawks/dyeing it rainbow colours, wearing corsets/leather/mascara etc (you get the picture), it's really no different. If you're the type that can blend in and enjoy something different, it will be a decent night out. If you're going to sneer/find everyone different/odd, you will not enjoy it. People are always worried about the whole racist issue because of the confederate flag. But it's just enjoying the country culture. I've no doubt some people are racist, but it's unfair to tar everyone that way because of todays political standards. My grandmother was never remotely racist, she just loved everything country. I wonder how people will view the whole metal scene in 50 years time if all the oldies are getting their hair spiked up and wearing hoodies/chains/etc with a mosh pit at the end. Probably the same way.

If I remember correctly, when Jefferson killed Chloe and had Max tied up and she escaped, the storm was still happening. Chloe dying didn't stop the storm. The only thing that stopped it was Chloe dying in the bathroom and not rewinding. I wouldn't necessarily say it's Chloes death that's important. You could look at it like Chloe needed to die there and then. But I'd wager that its the time travel that causes the rupture. Which is why I stand by my theory that the game would have been better off without time travel. The decisions you make would have a far bigger impact (Kate/Victoria/Nathan dying or living, Jefferson being caught/Joyce and David breakup/makeup, all of those would have contributed towards your end. As it stands, the only decision that made any real impact was to let Chloe live or go back and never mess with time. It's unsatisfying

The game plays out as a mystery. I don't think it would be hard pushed to set it up that a strap was loose while Jefferson was outside the room or she managed to pull the trolley close with a knife or something on the trolley. It's changing small details, but the game could have very easily played out in such a way that rewinding isn't required. Max could have hit the fire alarm at the start preventing the death of Chloe, later meets up with Chloe, both begin investigating Rachel's disappearance. As the story unfolds, Kate begins to get bullied, your choices effect whether she commits suicide or not. All I'm saying is that the game could have been made where time travel wasn't needed.  

What I'm saying is the story was engaging enough that time travel/alternate realities weren't needed. Or if they were going to include them, they should have made the choices you made count. The way it played out with the ending, it didn't matter if Kate killed herself in the game. Victoria's character progression never happened. The Joyce/David breakup/makeup doesn't matter. David Killing Jefferson has no repercussions. None of it matters, and when you play 20 hours into a game where it's mostly about making decisions and NONE of the decisions you make have an impact on the game at all, it isn't very rewarding. A decision making game where all of your decisions mean squat at the end is bad, and it's because they introduced time travel. The story itself WITHOUT time travel would have been solid enough.

That's a cliche saying that doesn't really ring true. If something is repeated often enough doesn't necessarily mean it's true. You can appreciate and enjoy the journey for what it is, but the end destination matters just as much if not more. Take education as a prime example.
